svg.text: ☁ AWS Application Flow Diagrams — Use Cases
USE CASE 1 — REST API with Caching (Standard Web App)
📊 CloudWatch Logs + Metrics + Alarms → SNS → PagerDuty | IAM Role on ECS Task → no hardcoded credentials
USE CASE 2 — Async Export Pipeline (Background Job)
📊 CloudWatch: SQS queue depth alarm → ECS Auto Scaling | VisibilityTimeout > max job processing time | Idempotency: skip duplicate messageIds
Each SQS subscriber decouples independently — Email service failure doesn't affect Billing. Each queue has its own DLQ and retry policy.
Filter policy on SNS → SQS: subscribe only to events matching criteria (e.g., only process orders from specific region)
SQS VisibilityTimeout must be > max processing time. If Lambda times out, message reappears and retries until DLQ threshold.
Security Group: ECS ← ALB only (port 8080) | RDS ← ECS only (port 5432) | Redis ← ECS only (port 6379)
USE CASE 5 — Serverless (Lambda + API Gateway + DynamoDB)
Cold start: Lambda inactive → JVM init ~1-2s (Java). Mitigate: provisioned concurrency, SnapStart (Java 21), keep-warm pings, use lighter runtimes (Node/Python).
When to choose Lambda over ECS: event-driven, short bursts <15 min, no persistent state, low traffic. ECS for: long-running, high throughput, stateful connections (DB pool).
DynamoDB access pattern first rule: model tables around queries, not entities. GSI for alternate query paths. Avoid scans.
USE CASE 6 — CI/CD Pipeline (Code to ECS Fargate)
Blue/Green: CodeDeploy shifts traffic from old (blue) to new (green) gradually. Instant rollback by rerouting ALB to blue target group.
Task definition update: new image tag → new task def revision → ECS service update → rolling replace or blue/green via CodeDeploy.
Secrets: never bake into image. Inject via ECS Task Definition → Secrets Manager ARN → container env var at runtime.
